title: PostgreSQL Join Strategies: Nested Loop, Hash Join, and Merge Join
realWorldScenario: While reviewing query plans across your application, you observe that joining `customers` (50,000 rows) and `orders` (2,000,000 rows) sometimes uses a Nested Loop, sometimes a Hash Join, and occasionally a Merge Join.
questionStatement: Analyze the three fundamental join algorithms in the PostgreSQL query engine: Nested Loop (with and without index), Hash Join, and Merge Join. Detail the memory prerequisites (`work_mem`), sort requirements, time complexity, and the specific cost trade-offs that drive the optimizer’s choice.
expectedConcepts: Nested loop optimal for tiny outer set + indexed inner lookup
Hash join builds hash table in work_mem and probes with outer scan
Multi-batch hash join spilling to disk when exceeding work_mem
Merge join requires pre-sorted inputs (B-tree or explicit sort)
Time complexity comparison across all three
hints: Which join strategy builds an in-memory hash table on the smaller table?
Which join requires both inputs to be sorted on the join key first?
What happens when a Hash Join exceeds work_mem?
